# Historical evidence synthesis: Scene external follow-up

## Scope and coverage

This report covers batch 1 of 1 for `scene_rsi_pilot__external_followup`: two supplied student-trajectory files, S0098 and S0099. The inventory lists 18 JSONL units for each. The supplied audit reports cover S0098 in two chunks and S0099 in one; this synthesis relies on those reports rather than reinspection of raw trajectories or image pixels. Paths below identify the original sources, and line numbers refer to their JSONL events. File counts can include copies and must not be treated as counts of independent trials.

- **S0098:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/external_followup/scene_rsi_pilot/selected/external_followup/bw_0011/trajectory.jsonl`
- **S0099:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/external_followup/fixed_h0/selected/external_followup/bw_0011/trajectory.jsonl`

## Evidence matrix

| Source and attempt | Executed behavior and feedback | Status and limits |
|---|---|---|
| S0098, step 1, lines 3–7 | Constructed named architectural and furnishing components; execution reported `ok: true`, 16 samples and PNG and blend saves. Step 1 was selected twice. | Operational build/render success; object visibility, connections and visual fidelity were not independently verified. |
| S0098, step 2, lines 8–14 | Following a comparison prompt, the student estimated anchor discrepancies and pale surfaces, then revised lighting and world settings; it also retained the door nodes returned by `include`. Execution again reported `ok: true`, 16 samples and saves; step 2 was selected twice. | Operational success and an executed revision, but no independently observed improvement or formal evaluation. Camera parameters remained unchanged. |
| S0098, next call, lines 15–18 | Reference and two renders were staged; the next student call timed out after approximately 600 seconds with zero tool calls, and the scene loop propagated the timeout. | Technical interruption. The second step was the stated fallback, but no subsequent answer, third execution or final submission is visible. |
| S0099, execution 1, lines 3–5 | The program failed at cabinet glass because a `.085` fillet exceeded half the `.018` thickness; no image was returned. | Observed build failure, not an empty patch. Code after the failure was not reached. |
| S0099, execution 2, lines 6, 8–10 | After receiving the traceback, the student reduced the pane fillet to `.008` and changed the cabinet body construction. The run timed out after approximately 600 seconds with empty logs and no image. | Technical timeout; completion of the fillet fix and the timeout’s cause are unknown. |
| S0099, execution 3 and later revision, lines 11, 13–18 | After timeout feedback, the student replaced many mural tubes with shared planar ribbons and lowered requested samples. The run failed during material assignment because `ob.data` was `None`. With no executions remaining, the student supplied a type and non-null guard. | A second observed build failure; the final correction was unexecuted. The performance change was an unvalidated hypothesis. |

## Comparison and interpretation

Both trajectories pursued an editable clean-laboratory reconstruction with architecture, cabinet, mural, display and services, under a runner that controlled saving and rendering (S0098 line 1; S0099 line 1). Constructing named owners and parts is evidence of intended scene structure, not proof that the objects were visible, correctly attached, editable as intended or visually faithful. Neither audit supplies the image pixels needed to independently assess the render against the reference.

S0098 demonstrates two operationally successful builds followed by interruption, not verified overall task success. Its comparison-driven revision is observable, but the student’s pale-surface diagnosis, estimated anchor discrepancies and predicted lighting effect remain hypotheses (lines 8–14; line 15 history). The unchanged camera and unresolved discrepancies are important limits on any claim that the revision corrected the scene. S0099 provides a contrasting sequence: explicit dimensional and object-data errors, an intervening timeout of unknown cause, and a final program that was never executed (lines 3–18). Its failure cannot be generalized into a claim about the quality of a completed render, because none was returned.

Neither trajectory shows an empty patch, permission stop, branch stop or CLI stop. The observed stops are instead S0098’s later session timeout and S0099’s runner timeout, alongside S0099’s actual build errors. These categories should not be conflated with one another or with formal task failure.

## Teacher and feedback evidence

No identifiable teacher advice, diagnosis or proposed update is visible in either supplied trajectory; consequently, neither receipt nor adoption of separate teacher advice is established. S0098 did receive user comparison and scheduling instructions and made an observable revision after them (lines 8–10); that is not evidence of a teacher intervention. S0099 received runner traceback and timeout feedback and autonomously changed its program (lines 6–15); runner feedback is not teacher advice. No teacher acceptance or independently observed quality judgment is shown. The successful S0098 executions validate that those runs completed, not that the scene or the lighting change was accepted as correct.

## Transferable constraints and uncertainties

- **Execution and visual correctness are distinct.** S0098’s saved outputs show why successful rendering alone cannot verify framing, occlusion, support, contacts, materials or reference fidelity. S0099 is a counterexample to assuming a specified scene was even fully constructed: its first run stopped before later code was reached.
- **Runtime constraints and validation matter.** S0099’s fillet dimensions and null object data produced concrete failures, while its later guard remains untested. Its ribbon consolidation may or may not have addressed the timeout; the observed cause was not established. The specific dimensions and mural implementation are task-specific, not universal thresholds.
- **Lighting and geometry claims need observation.** S0098’s pale-surface diagnosis and lighting adjustment are task-specific hypotheses, not demonstrated improvements. Both audits also describe additional illumination beyond the requested LED-only lighting (S0098 lines 3–4; S0099 lines 9–10 and 14–15), without establishing the resulting appearance.

Formal scores and final visual quality are unknown for both sources. No causal superiority between the trajectories follows from these records, and old model cost cannot be recovered from its absence. This synthesis is audit-only and does not enter capability generation.
